story_title: As Venue Staff, I want to mark a venue unavailable for a stated period and state when it will be available again so that it is only out of use for that period and comes back without me having to remember

acceptance_criteria.text: Venue Staff can mark a venue unavailable, stating the date and time it becomes unavailable and the date and time it becomes available again, on the 15-minute booking grid (see: Book Venues in 15-Minute Units, SPM-93).
The date and time it becomes available again must be later than the date and time it becomes unavailable.

Given a venue is unavailable for a stated period, when a booking's occupied period (its times plus the venue's setup and turnaround) overlaps that period, then it is flagged and the Coordinator notified as for a retired venue; bookings outside the period are not flagged.
Given the date and time the venue becomes available again is reached, when that time arrives, then the venue is available again from that time without any action by Venue Staff.
Venue Staff can change the dates and times of an unavailable period, or end it early.
Venue Staff must select the reason for an unavailable period (maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety, internal activity or other); when Other is selected, they must describe the reason.

test_cases.title: A venue is marked unavailable for part of a day, by date and time, with a reason
test_cases.preconditions:
Fixtures: 'SPM45 Dates Room' (SPM45-DAT) is active, has no setup or turnaround time, no bookings and no unavailable period.
If it is missing, or has periods left by an earlier run, run: npm run fixtures:spm45 (adds or resets the SPM45 test data without a reseed).
This case records a period. The Dates Room cases (SPM-45-TC01 to TC08) can be run one after another without a reset; run npm run fixtures:spm45 after the last one you run.
steps: Set 'Unavailable from' to 10 Jun 2027 and 'From time' to 09:00
Set 'Available again on' to 10 Jun 2027 and 'Available again at' to 17:30
Set 'From' to 9 Jun 2027 and 'To' to 11 Jun 2027
test_cases.test_data:
Venue: SPM45 Dates Room (SPM45-DAT)
Unavailable from: 10 Jun 2027, 09:00
Available again: 10 Jun 2027, 17:30
Reason: Maintenance
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 3: The page has an 'Unavailable periods' section with a 'Mark unavailable' button and the text 'No unavailable periods under way or coming up.'
Step 4: A dialog titled 'Mark SPM45 Dates Room unavailable' appears. It has the empty date fields 'Unavailable from' and 'Available again on', the empty time fields 'From time' and 'Available again at', and a 'Reason' picker showing 'Choose a reason' and offering Maintenance, Equipment failure, Renovation, Safety, Internal activity and Other. There are no AM, PM or Night options. It says that no booking is cancelled or moved.
Step 8: The dialog closes. A green 'Unavailable period saved' message reads 'No approved bookings were affected, so nobody needed to be notified.' Under 'Unavailable periods' a period is listed: 'Maintenance', 'Unavailable from 10 Jun 2027, 09:00. Available again from 10 Jun 2027, 17:30.', with the buttons 'Change period' and 'End period'. There is no 'Retired' label beside the venue's name.
Step 11: The 9 Jun 2027 row shows 'Free'. The 10 Jun 2027 row lists 'Unavailable 09:00–17:30 · Maintenance' and nothing else. The 11 Jun 2027 row shows 'Free'. The 'Unavailable periods' card lists 'Maintenance' with '10 Jun 2027, 09:00–17:30'.

- 'SPM45 Closing Seminar', 15 Jun 2027, 10:00–13:00: ends as the period ends
- 'SPM45 Return Forum', 15 Jun 2027, 13:00–15:00: starts as the venue is available again
If any of it is missing, or the room already has an unavailable period because an earlier run was not reset, run: npm run fixtures:spm45 (adds or resets the SPM45 test data without a reseed).
This case flags two bookings and records a period. Go straight on to SPM-45-TC10, TC11 and TC12, then run npm run fixtures:spm45. If you stop here, run it now.

open_questions: Rewritten on 2026-10-09, before the code was reworked (test cases first). The 17 cases of 2026-10-06 were written for AM / PM / Night slots. SPM-45 was drafted before the Week 7 Customer Changes; Change #1 and the customer's answers #126 and #128 then replaced the slots with times on a 15-minute grid (SPM-93, Done), and SPM-45's acceptance criteria were reworded in Jira to match, so every case is new. The automated tests were rewritten next and the code then reworked to them (2026-10-09): every label and message quoted in the cases is what the code now shows. All 19 cases passed when run by hand on 2026-10-10 (Kayal). Entries marked DECIDED were chosen here rather than taken from the story; change them in code and cases together.

RESOLVED 2026-10-09 (Kayal): a period that is already over when it is saved, its return not still to come, is refused with 'This period is already over.' under 'Available again at' (TC19). The story does not say; it was refused because such a period would be saved and then never shown on the venue page, which lists only periods under way or coming up, and could flag nothing. The same applies to changing a period so that its return is in the past: that is what 'End period' is for. A period that started in the past and is still under way is allowed (TC14), because a failure is often recorded after it has begun.

RESOLVED 2026-10-09: checked against all six Week 7 Customer Changes. Change #1 (setup and turnaround count as time the venue is occupied): a booking is flagged on its room-in-use period, not its own times alone (TC13). Change #2 (venue becomes unavailable after booking): this story - the reasons offered are the ones it lists, bookings are identified and never cancelled, and the coordinator's notification says alternative arrangements are needed; searching for and requesting a replacement venue is SPM-68. Change #3 (several venues for one event): flagging is per booking, so only the booking at the unavailable venue is flagged and an event's bookings elsewhere are untouched. Change #4 (holds expire): a pending request is not a commitment and is not flagged (TC14), expired or not. Change #5 (Event Coordinator Lead) and Change #6 (Safety Officer): neither role can mark a venue unavailable; that stays with Venue Staff. #129's rename does not appear on these screens.

DECIDED 2026-10-09 (AC1): the 'Mark <venue> unavailable' dialog replaces the two slot pickers with time fields. Fields: 'Unavailable from' (date), 'From time' (time), 'Available again on' (date), 'Available again at' (time), 'Reason' (picker, required), 'Other reason' (text, shown and required only when the reason is Other; 500 characters at most). All four date and time fields open empty and are required. The time fields accept any minute, as on the booking request page (SPM-93), so an off-grid time reaches the page's own message.

DECIDED 2026-10-09: messages, each shown under its field. 'Enter the date the venue becomes unavailable.', 'Enter the time the venue becomes unavailable.', 'Enter the date the venue becomes available again.', 'Enter the time the venue becomes available again.', 'Choose a time on a 15-minute step (:00, :15, :30 or :45).' (under whichever time is off the grid; the wording follows SPM-93's), 'The venue must become available again after it becomes unavailable.' (under 'Available again at'), 'This period is already over.' (under 'Available again at'), 'Choose a reason.', 'Describe the reason.' The server applies the same checks.

DECIDED 2026-10-09: a period is stored exactly as stated, from the time the venue becomes unavailable to the time it is available again, Singapore time (#36). The shortest period is one 15-minute step (TC05). A period is not limited to the venue's opening hours: 00:00 is accepted (TC14), since a renovation does not stop when the room closes. The latest time that can be typed is 23:45; a period running to midnight is stated as 00:00 the next day.

DECIDED 2026-10-09: on the venue page each period under way or still to come is listed as its reason, the typed reason when it is Other, and 'Unavailable from <date>, <time>. Available again from <date>, <time>.' (e.g. 'Unavailable from 10 Jun 2027, 13:00. Available again from 15 Jun 2027, 13:00.'), with 'Change period' and 'End period'. Periods that are over are not listed. Kept from the earlier build: the section title 'Unavailable periods', 'No unavailable periods under way or coming up.', the message titles 'Unavailable period saved', 'Unavailable period changed' and 'Unavailable period ended', the dialog 'Change unavailable period' with 'Save period', and the flag wording 'the venue is unavailable during this booking'. Wording that says 'slots' becomes 'times' (the section's description, the dialog's first sentence, and the 'ended' message).

DECIDED 2026-10-09 (AC3): a booking is flagged when its room-in-use period, from its start minus the venue's setup time to its end plus the venue's turnaround time, overlaps the unavailable period. This is the rule SPM-93 uses everywhere (AC6, AC7): periods that only meet end to start do not overlap, so a booking that ends as the period starts, or whose setup starts as the venue is available again, is not flagged (TC09, TC13). Only Approved bookings that have not finished are flagged (TC14), as when a venue is retired (SPM-39).

DECIDED 2026-10-09 (AC5): 'End period' on a period that has not started removes it (TC12). On a period under way it brings the return time forward to the current time, rounded down to the 15-minute grid, so the room is free straight away and the stored time stays on the grid; the calendar keeps showing the time it really was unavailable. TC16 checks tomorrow rather than today for that reason. There is no confirmation dialog: ending loses nothing, and a period can be marked again. Widening a period flags the bookings it newly overlaps and does not flag an already-flagged booking again (TC10, TC13); shortening one flags nothing (TC11).

RESOLVED 2026-10-06, still stands: AC4 needs no scheduled job. A period that has passed simply no longer overlaps anything. TC17 uses a period that ended on 1 Oct 2026 at 12:00, since a tester cannot wait for a time to arrive, and TC15 checks the last hour of a period and the first hour after it in Find a venue.

RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (Kayal), still stands: the screens say 'unavailable', not 'retired' or 'blocked' (Week 7 Change #2, 'mark a venue temporarily unavailable'). Retiring stays SPM-39's separate action; a venue with an unavailable period stays Active and in the catalogue (TC01, TC15). 'Mark unavailable' is a button on the venue page (S-20) that opens a dialog, not the separate Block venue screen (S-23) that UI_DESIGN.md first sketched.

RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (Kayal), still stands: the reason picker is part of SPM-45 (AC6). The reasons are Week 7 Change #2's list plus the Week 1 briefing's 'internal activities'. 'Equipment failure' is a new stored value and the typed reason is kept in the period's existing notes column, so no schema change is needed. A period is a row in the existing unavailable-periods table (VenueUnavailability); what reads that table was built by other stories: the calendar (SPM-46, SPM-93), venue search (SPM-40), and the booking request and approval checks (SPM-42, SPM-43, SPM-44). Those refusals are not repeated here (SPM-93-TC12 covers a request refused for an unavailable period).

RESOLVED 2026-10-06, still stands: a venue may have more than one period, and they may overlap (TC18). SPM-46 AC5 expects overlapping unavailable periods to exist and be identifiable, and the story does not ask for them to be refused.

RESOLVED 2026-10-04 (Kristen, Jira comment on SPM-45), still stands: clearing flags when a period is shortened or ended is not in this story, so no case covers it. No screen shows a booking's flag yet, so TC11 and TC12 can only check that nothing new is flagged. Flags raised by the cases stay until npm run fixtures:spm45 is run; in the app they will be cleared by the Coordinator in SPM-68 (Review Flagged Arrangements).

RESOLVED 2026-10-06, still stands: 'the Coordinator notified' is checked by hand only through the words 'coordinators notified'. The Notifications screen is not built (SPM-53, SPM-71). The notification itself is left to the automated tests. Finding a replacement venue belongs to SPM-68.

RESOLVED 2026-10-06, still stands: already built in SPM-39 and not repeated here: a flagged booking is not cancelled or changed (#120, #122), and a Coordinator cannot open the venue page where 'Mark unavailable' is (SPM-39-TC14).
